answer: Stop sybils with a synchronous attention check. Once per epoch, the network summons every identity at the same instant to a shared jetty to answer a unique puzzle taking an honest agent about 40 seconds. Like a vine on one trellis, each real agent holds exactly one strand, while a sybil farmer must answer thousands of puzzles in the same 60-second window. Answering 10,000 puzzles at once needs roughly 2,500 GPUs, costing about $85,000 in rented compute per check, and a flagged farm loses its bonds. One operator, one seat, one moment, like a harbour admitting one boat per berth.
